experiences.G0: Schema-first: Query `information_schema.columns` with no LIKE filter to see all columns; confirm exact names, join keys, and unique constraints before writing any query.
experiences.G1: Cast-before-sort: Always CAST VARCHAR numeric columns to FLOAT/DOUBLE in SQL ORDER BY to prevent lexicographic misranking.
experiences.G2: SQL over LLM: Use pure SQL for structured filters, joins, aggregates, entity lookups, categorical strings, and any fixed-template derivations; reserve LLM only for genuinely unstructured semantic reasoning.
experiences.G3: SQL-only default: When a filter attribute is absent from the primary table, query `information_schema.columns` across ALL tables including LIKE '%date%' variants; enumerate all columns before substituting proxies or world knowledge.
experiences.G4: LLM scope: Verify pure SQL resolves the question first; exhaust all related tables before invoking llm_map/llm_reduce; pre-filter with all available SQL constraints to smallest non-null candidate set (≤20 rows) to minimize token cost.
experiences.G5: Parameter validation: Confirm all required llm_map/llm_reduce parameters (including key_column when using key_strategy='by_row_id') before execution; test on a 1-row sample to catch API errors early.
experiences.G6: Verify-before-filter: Run DISTINCT SQL on all candidate columns to confirm exact label values, NULL counts, encoding schemes, denominator scope, and date/lookup column existence before writing the main query or invoking any LLM operator.
experiences.G7: Filter-then-aggregate: Apply all row-reducing SQL filters and FK joins before any LLM operators or aggregates; SQL filtering is O(1) cost vs. O(n) token cost for row-level LLM classification.
experiences.G8: Single-table sufficiency: Before joining tables, verify whether a single-table SELECT (including url/link fields) already contains the answer; avoid unnecessary joins or redundant schema checks.
experiences.G9: Schema verification depth: Run `SELECT * LIMIT 1` and `information_schema.columns` on every relevant table; if LIKE searches fail after 2-3 attempts, use row preview to visually identify relevant columns before further exploration.
experiences.G10: Single SQL execution: Combine retrieval and output in one run_sql call; never repeat an identical query to save results, as redundant calls inflate cost without benefit.
experiences.G11: Deterministic literal: For finite well-known mappings (ZIP→city, id→name), query related tables first to confirm names; only use SQL CASE/literals after DB verification to eliminate token cost.
experiences.G12: Deduplicate before LLM: When a join key is missing, scan for name-bearing tables as semantic proxies; only apply LLM to the minimal unique candidate set when no join path exists.
experiences.G13: Early pivot: After confirming a column is absent across all tables, attempt structural SQL workarounds (range joins, sequence tables) before switching to LLM world-knowledge calls.
experiences.G14: Proxy rejection: Never substitute a coarser field without exhausting all direct table inspection methods; confirm column absence with a targeted per-table schema query before accepting absence or invoking LLM inference.
experiences.G15: Consolidate discovery: Issue one broad `information_schema.columns` query across ALL tables at workflow start, including space-aware LIKE variants for multi-word names; never repeat the same schema inspection method.
experiences.G16: LLM as last resort: Never use LLM operators for structured data retrieval, numeric aggregates, entity lookups, fixed-rule derivations, or SQL-expressible checks; LLM produces incomplete results at O(n) token cost vs. O(1) SQL.
experiences.G17: Batch LLM calls: Issue one comprehensive prompt with all available context; only invoke llm_reduce when input data contains query-relevant information, otherwise switch SQL approach.
experiences.G18: Preserve cardinality: Never use SELECT DISTINCT when the query requires one output row per source record; deduplicate only when unique entities are explicitly requested.
experiences.G19: Filter-then-expand: Apply all row-reducing SQL filters before joining or expanding; if results are unexpectedly few, relax filters (e.g., LEFT JOIN, remove rtype) to diagnose exclusions.
experiences.G20: Rowid/LAG caution: Only use rowid/LAG heuristics after verifying insertion order and rowid count matches target PK range; if group counts mismatch entity counts, immediately abandon and explore alternative linkages.
experiences.G21: Nested-window avoidance: Never use ordering-based heuristics on unsorted data without verifying sort order; materialize LAG in a CTE first, then apply aggregation in a subsequent step.
experiences.G22: Early row-count check: When a JOIN or filter returns fewer rows than expected, run NULL checks and join-coverage diagnostics on base tables to confirm data existence before accepting or abandoning results.
experiences.G23: Output-type check: Before finalizing SQL, verify whether the question requires a scalar aggregate (rate, percentage, count) or per-row values to avoid metric misinterpretation.
experiences.G24: Batch overwrite guard: Run LLM classification once on the full filtered dataset; use INSERT INTO (not CREATE OR REPLACE) across all batches to avoid overwriting prior results; verify total row coverage before aggregating.
experiences.G25: Proxy cardinality check: Verify a filter's row count on the base table before joining; a shortfall in final results is immediately detectable when pre-join counts are known.
experiences.G26: Join-key validation: After multi-table joins, verify key overlap (COUNT of unmatched keys) to catch missing records due to key mismatches before accepting results.
experiences.G27: Range-overlap filter: For range queries, use overlap logic (low <= Y AND high >= X) not exact equality to avoid silently excluding valid partial-range records.
experiences.G28: Range-column preference: Prefer pre-aggregated range columns over Low/High equality filters, which silently exclude records with partial range overlap.
experiences.G29: NULL-result rejection: Never alias a confirmed-NULL column as a substitute for a missing one; join the table that actually holds the data or try alternative column names before accepting NULL.
experiences.G30: Domain-table priority: For domain-specific metrics, check the most relevant domain table first for pre-computed values before deriving from raw data.
experiences.G31: Tie-breaking order: When ranking produces ties, explicitly verify which tiebreaker rule matches expected output, then apply a deterministic secondary sort key (e.g., lowest ID, alphabetical) for reproducible results.
experiences.G32: Monthly-average denominator: When computing monthly averages over a fixed calendar year, always divide total by 12, not by the count of months with non-zero data.
experiences.G33: Avoid LLM confirmation: Never use llm_reduce to interpret, confirm, or cross-validate a result already computed by SQL; treat SQL results as authoritative and discard redundant LLM calls.
experiences.G34: Value-range validation: When a column's name is ambiguous or absent, use MIN/MAX/AVG profiling to infer semantic meaning before applying LLM operators or accepting schema absence.
experiences.G35: SQL arithmetic: Express derived metrics (e.g., COUNT(*)/12.0 for monthly averages) directly in SQL rather than post-processing to keep solutions pure-SQL and token-free.
experiences.G36: Fail-fast probe: Verify a table's schema once; if metadata looks suspicious, immediately run the actual SQL query — SQL errors are more reliable than repeated metadata checks.
experiences.G37: Sample-bias risk: Never aggregate LLM-imputed values over a partial sample; filter to exact target rows before any LLM inference to avoid compounding sampling and hallucination errors.
experiences.G38: Focused world-knowledge query: Combine all needed context (entities, year, specific request) into one precise LLM call rather than iterating with vague or partial prompts.
experiences.G39: Step budget: Cap schema exploration and heuristic attempts at 5 steps total; if no clear path emerges, immediately commit to the best available approximation and reserve a step for the final answer.
experiences.G40: FK-first joins: Before using world-knowledge CASE heuristics, verify all FK columns exist via schema inspection and use direct joins; query `duckdb_constraints()` and scan ALL tables for FK references before abandoning SQL joins.
experiences.G41: Explicit answer output: Always output a best-effort final answer as the last step; ensure internal reasoning matches the written result — a correct inference left unrecorded scores as wrong.
experiences.G42: ID-join enforcement: Always attempt SQL join for ID-to-name resolution before LLM operators; LLM world-knowledge mapping is unreliable, costly, and produces incomplete results.
experiences.G43: Result completeness check: When a filtered query returns fewer rows than expected, investigate missing records via relaxed filters or LEFT JOIN before accepting the result.
experiences.G44: Answer-column check: Before finalizing, confirm output columns match the question's exact required format (URL, name, number, coordinates); reject related-but-incomplete or wrong field types.
experiences.G45: Coordinate column probe: For location tasks, run a broad `information_schema.columns` scan then narrow to `%lat%/%lng%/%coord%`; if absent after one scan, pivot immediately to LLM world-knowledge inference.
experiences.G46: Recency filter: When a question references a named event, filter by MAX(year) or latest date to return the most recent instance, not the first match.
experiences.G47: URL-first lookup: When a URL or structured value is needed, immediately SELECT all columns from the entity table to check for existing fields before any joins or LLM calls.
experiences.G48: Early termination: Once a plausible target column is confirmed and returns a result, immediately finalize and submit the answer; never continue schema validation loops after a viable column is identified.
experiences.G49: Key normalization: When key lengths or types differ across tables, fix format discrepancies immediately in SQL (e.g., LPAD, SUBSTR, TRIM, CAST) rather than attempting post-hoc lookups or workarounds.
experiences.G50: Diagnostic pivot: When a join or column SELECT produces zero/unexpected matches, immediately attempt the complete multi-table JOIN rather than decomposing into individual column probes.
experiences.G51: Cardinality anchor: When SQL confirms exactly N matching rows, treat that count as a hard constraint and prefer structural SQL recovery over full-table LLM classification.
experiences.G52: NULL-aware ranking: In top-N queries, use LEFT JOIN with NULLS LAST ordering to avoid silently dropping valid candidates; only add IS NOT NULL if the task explicitly excludes missing values.
experiences.G53: Proxy-mapping risk: Never map a domain term to a semantically unrelated column (e.g., `attacking_work_rate` for `preferred_foot`) without explicit schema evidence; wrong proxies guarantee incorrect results.
experiences.G54: Sanity-check anchors: After forming a domain hypothesis, cross-validate via COUNT(*) against known totals before committing to that filter; also cross-validate key results against an unfiltered query to confirm the result is not a filter artifact.
experiences.G55: Zero-result trust: When schema mapping is validated via DISTINCT inspection and the query executes cleanly, accept a zero result as correct; use restrictive filter interpretation to avoid inflated counts.
experiences.G56: Sanity-count check: After inferring a filter or join, compare COUNT(*) vs COUNT(DISTINCT id) to detect duplication, then spot-check before running the full aggregation.
experiences.G57: Aggregation order: For 'average across subjects per school,' compute per-subject averages first, then average those; cross-check with row-level average to confirm correct interpretation.
experiences.G58: Permissive averaging: Use COALESCE or NULL-ignoring aggregation when averaging across multiple score columns to avoid excluding records with partial data.
experiences.G59: Aggregation consistency: Always compute AVG()/SUM() in SQL rather than returning a raw stored column value to match the correct aggregation level required by the question.
experiences.G60: Join-then-sort: For min/max metric queries, JOIN relevant tables, apply filters, ORDER BY the metric, and LIMIT 1 rather than using subqueries or LLM ranking.
experiences.G61: Range-boundary inference: Avoid positional or range-boundary heuristics to infer foreign keys; one misidentified column corrupts all downstream results; prefer explicit FK or schema evidence.
experiences.G62: LLM-input readability: Before calling llm_reduce, verify the target column contains human-readable text, not bare numeric IDs, to ensure meaningful LLM output.
experiences.G63: Verify-LLM-facts: After LLM generates precise numeric facts (coordinates, dates, measurements), run a SQL consistency check to catch hallucinated or inaccurate values before finalizing.
experiences.G64: Distinct-join count: When counting entities through a bridge/junction table join, always use COUNT(DISTINCT entity_id) to prevent duplicate inflation from multiple join matches.
experiences.G65: LLM-retry avoidance: If an LLM operator fails, diagnose parameter format before retrying; limit to 1 retry with a corrected prompt, then pivot to a cheaper SQL or llm_reduce alternative rather than repeating the same failing call.
experiences.G66: ID-age fallacy: Never use MAX/MIN of a surrogate ID as a proxy for age; always locate a dedicated date/birth column before ranking by age.
experiences.G67: Knowledge fallback: When SQL confirms a column or value is absent, apply LLM-known facts directly as SQL constants (e.g., hardcoded date filters); never use llm_reduce to guess database facts it cannot access.
experiences.G68: Combine LLM attributes: When inferring multiple missing columns via world knowledge, issue one llm_map call with a combined prompt to extract all needed attributes simultaneously.
experiences.G69: Preview-truncation caution: Never trust `preview_relation` alone for schema completeness; always cross-check with `SELECT * FROM table LIMIT 1` and attempt full JOIN SQL before concluding a column is absent.
experiences.G70: Error-triggered re-inspection: A column-not-found SQL error must trigger exact schema re-inspection of the target table, not immediate LLM fallback over the full dataset.
experiences.G71: Template-SQL construction: When output follows a known string pattern (e.g., URL from year/name), use SQL string concatenation instead of LLM operators to eliminate token cost and format mismatches.
experiences.G72: Rate denominator check: Before computing a completion/success rate, enumerate distinct status values and confirm whether the denominator is all entrants or only starters to avoid definitional errors.
experiences.G73: Status-rate SQL: Compute completion/success rates as COUNT(CASE WHEN status='X' THEN 1 END)/COUNT(*)*100 directly in SQL; never return per-row breakdowns for scalar rate questions.
experiences.G74: Date-join filter: When filtering by a specific event date, confirm the target ID by joining on an actual date column rather than relying on external calendar knowledge.
experiences.G75: Unique join keys: When joining llm_map output back to source data, always join on a unique primary key, never on the classified value column which may contain duplicates.
